title: Messages — all our notifications in one place
body:
On the **„Messages”** tab you will find all our system notifications in one place — invoice
notices, payment reminders, news about your website, by both e-mail and SMS — and this is
also where **guest enquiries coming from your website** arrive.

![Screenshot: the Messages tab on a phone](assets/hu/screen.png)

## What is this good for?

If one of our e-mails ended up in the spam folder, or an SMS arrived on a different phone,
you can still find it here. You do not need to search through your mailbox.

## Guest enquiries from your website

If a guest fills in the booking enquiry card on your website (dates, number of people, name,
contact details), we send an e-mail about it to your contact address, and the enquiry also
appears here, among the Messages — the guest's name, e-mail address or phone number is in
the body of the message.

**It is up to you to act:** an enquiry is not yet a booking — reply to the guest using the
contact details they provided. If the guest gave an e-mail address, you can also reply to
our e-mail with the „Reply” button of your e-mail program: in that case the reply goes
directly to the guest. If they only gave a phone number, call them or send an SMS. The
sooner you reply, the greater the chance that the enquirer becomes a guest.

## Which channel did it arrive on?

On every row, under the date (next to the date on a desktop computer) you can see the name
of the channel: **„Email”** or **„SMS”**. You do not need to filter for it — just by
reading through the list you can see which message we sent by e-mail and which to your
phone.

## What is current and what is no longer?

Some of our messages are about the **status** of your account, and a later one may override
them. The most typical case is the series of payment reminders: first „Esedékes a
honlapdíj” (Website fee due), then „Your website is suspended”,
and finally — if you have settled the fee — „Your website is back online” (Your website is
available again).

We call such consecutive notifications a **thread**: the successive turns of one and the
same matter — your subscription, a particular booking request, the multilingual version.
So that you do not have to work out which one is still valid:

- The **most recent** row of the thread gets a green label, and the label also **names
  what the thread is about**: „Ez a legfrissebb — **subscription**” (This is the latest —
  subscription), „Ez a legfrissebb — **booking request**” (This is the latest — booking
  request) or „Ez a legfrissebb — **multilingual module**” (This is the latest — multilingual
  module). Directly below it, it states **how many earlier messages it overrides** — for
  example „Overwrites 4 earlier message(s)”. You can safely
  ignore that many notifications: they no longer describe the current status.
  If it overrides exactly one, the row also **names it**: „1 korábbi üzenetet ír felül:
  »Foglalási kérés: Kis Anna, 2026. 09. 22.–2026. 09. 24.«” (Overrides 1 earlier message:
  »Booking request: Anna Kis, ...«).
  A stand-alone message does **not** get a green label — there is nothing to override.
- Whatever a later one has already overridden gets a **„Overdue”** (Superseded) label,
  with a fainter, struck-through title, and below it states **what overrode it** and when
  — for example „Overridden by: »Your website is back online« · 2026. 09. 12. 10:35”.

Superseded messages **do not disappear**: you can open and read them, we simply indicate
that they no longer describe the current status of your account.

### One matter — one row

A longer matter (for example a series of payment reminders) does **not take up 10 rows** in
the list. In the list stands its **most recent** message, and below it a toggle that tells
you how many earlier steps belong to it — for example:

> ▾ Earlier 44 steps of this same case — subscription

Tapping it **opens up the steps** (indented, tied to the matter), and the toggle's label
changes to „▴ Hide earlier steps”. Nothing is lost: the number
above the list still counts **all messages**, not the rows, and the **search also finds**
something that appears in a step of a collapsed matter.

Only genuine matters collapse: the turns of your subscription, the status of the
multilingual version, and the turns of **one particular** booking request. Invoice notices
remain separate rows — a new invoice does not make an old one untrue.

### Why do I see several green labels at once?

Because **several threads are running at the same time**, and each has its own most recent
message. This is not a contradiction: one says the final word about your subscription, the
other about a booking request. That is why the label names **which thread** it belongs to.

Several booking requests can run at once, so **two green labels may say the same thing**:
„This is the latest — booking request”. In that case
the **guest name and time** on the row, and the „1 korábbi üzenetet ír felül: »…«”
(Overrides 1 earlier message: »…«) line under the label, tell you which request it is — the
two rows are about two SEPARATE bookings, not two versions of the same request.

This marking applies to status messages (payment reminders, the readiness of the
multilingual version, and the turns of a particular booking request). An invoice notice,
your login details, or a separate guest enquiry **never gets such a label** — those are
independent facts, not newer versions of one another.

## Unread messages

In the menu on the left (in the bottom bar on a phone), next to the **„Messages”** label a
small number shows how many unread messages you have. In the list, unread rows stand out in
bolder type and with a coloured border.

⚠️ **A superseded message does NOT count as unread.** If a notification has already been
overridden by a later one (for example the „Your website is suspended” row by „Your website is back online”), the system treats it as a **closed matter** and does not alert you about it. So
the number shown in the menu reflects **how much still awaits you** — not how many e-mails
we have ever sent.

Tapping a message opens it in place, and at the same time marks it as read. On every row
there is a **„Open ▾”** indicator, and **„Close ▴”** when open. If
you want to mark several as read at once, the button above the list is for that — it
**only affects what is currently in the list according to the filter** (see below: *The
mark-as-read button*).

## Filtering and searching

Under the search box there are **three rows of buttons**, because they ask three separate
questions: *what it is about*, *how it arrived* and *what state it is in*. The three work
**together**.

### „What it is about” — the topic

If you have many booking notices, here you can bring up what you are looking for with one
tap. The buttons are mutually exclusive: exactly one topic is always active.

- **„All”** — all four topics, meaning no narrowing by topic.
- **„Bookings”** — booking requests and enquiries that came from your
  website, as well as cancellation/expiry notices.
- **„Billing”** — invoice notices and payment reminders.
- **„My website”** — news concerning your website: it is ready, your own web
  address, foreign-language versions, guest reviews, traffic report.
- **„Account”** — your login details and everything else.

⚠️ **„All”** only releases the TOPIC. If, for example, „Email” or „Unread” is switched on below it, or there is a word in the search box, those remain in
effect, and the list stays filtered. For the full list, the safest is the **„Clear filter”** link next to the search box — it releases everything with a
single tap, including the search word.

**The topic buttons carry a count.** This number always shows how many messages you would
get if you tapped it — that is, it already accounts for the narrowing set below it. If, for
example, **„Unread”** is switched on, the number next to „Billing”
is the count of unread billing messages.

### „How it arrived” — the channel

- **„Email”** — only our e-mails.
- **„SMS”** — only text messages.

### „State”

- **„Unread”** — what still awaits you.

These buttons **work together with the topic**: „Billing” and „Unread” can be switched on at the same time, so you see only unread billing messages.
Tapping an active button again switches it off.

**Every button carries a count** — the topic buttons, the channel buttons, and „Unread” too. If **0** stands next to any of them, that tells you in advance that you would
get an empty list: you do not have to tap it to find out.

⚠️ **The number on the „Unread” button and the number shown in the menu are
two different things.** In the menu (in the bottom bar on a phone), the number next to
„Messages” shows the unread items in your **entire** mailbox. The number on the
„Unread” button, however, **takes all your other settings into account** — the
selected topic, the channel and the search word too — which is why it is often smaller than
the one shown in the menu. Neither is wrong: the menu tells you how many there are in
total, the button how many you would get right now.

Above the list, a line always states **how many of all the messages you are seeing, and
what you have filtered for** — for example „77 / 114 üzenet — téma: Számlázás” (77 / 114
messages — topic: Billing).

### The mark-as-read button

The button **only affects what is currently in the list** — and the number in its label
tells you **how many UNREAD messages it affects** (not how many rows you see):

- Without a filter, the count follows the **„Mark as read”**
  label (for example „— 2 üzenet” / — 2 messages), even if 5 messages are showing in the
  list meanwhile. This number is the same as the one on the **„Unread”**
  button and the badge on the Messages tab.
- On a filtered list the button's label is also different: **„Mark the … filtered messages as read”** — followed by the count („2 üzenetet” / 2 messages).
  That is, it only affects those matching the filter, the unread items outside the filter
  remain untouched.

**A single tap does nothing irreversible:** the button first **asks** („Mark the next 2 messages as read?”), and under
the question it tells you whether it affects the entire mailbox or only the currently
filtered list. **„Cancel”** leaves everything as it was.

⚠️ After pressing the button, the list *grows back*: if the **„Unread”**
narrowing was switched on, it switches off by itself (otherwise the messages you just made
read would vanish from your sight). The topic, channel and search filters remain.

So, for example, you can first tap the **„Bookings”** topic and mark all
booking notices as read at once, while your billing messages remain unread — that is, in
plain sight.

If there are no unread messages among those matching the filter, the button disappears.

You can type any word into the search box: the interface searches both the subject and the
body of the message, and you do not have to get the accents exactly right („szamla” also
finds „számlát” / invoice). If you have filtered or searched, the **„Clear filter”** link takes you back to the full list.

## Attachments

If an invoice was attached to a message, you can download the PDF with the **„Download attachment”** button at the bottom of the opened message. The same
document is also available on the **„Documents”** tab.

## If the list is empty

We switched on the collection of messages in August 2026. Our e-mails earlier than that are
not shown here — they can only be found in your own e-mail mailbox.
